checks.reason: This replacement fixes the defect I flagged in the composed application review: an unmarked adoption of the variant. 'I am loath to kill you' renders the Tongjian's 恨恨不欲殺汝 fairly (恨恨 glossed as 相戀之情, lingering attachment, plus 不欲殺 'do not wish to kill'). It is no longer presented as the extant text: the bracket says it follows the Tongjian variant and gives the extant Jinshu reading as 'I regret not killing you'. That is the correct rendering of 恨不殺汝 and matches the approved literal. It reports the Jinshu Jiaozhu's 'probably corrupt' judgment, which reflects the commentary's 疑, without overstating it. It also points to the literal note, which holds both witnesses, including Yulan 744/Records of Former Yan 誓不殺汝. 'I have lived in your country for a long time' renders 吾處汝國久 accurately. The variant reading also fits the neighbouring speech (s0166–s0170), which threatens and then offers a test rather than killing. No Chinese is changed, nothing is silently emended, and no person, date or identity is affected.
checks.after: I have lived in your country for a long time, and I am loath to kill you [following the Tongjian variant; the extant Jinshu wording reads “I regret not killing you” and is judged probably corrupt in the Jinshu Jiaozhu; see the textual note in the literal translation].

cautions: This is an editorial review of English wording only. It is not approval of any date, identity, chapter or publication, and it does not clear any attribution or chronology hold.
